title: City man 'achieves teen dream' by creating AI girl group 'with millions' of fans
key_facts: Craig Raybould, 43, from Cannock near Birmingham, created Certain Call, a fictional AI R&B girl group.
Members are fictional characters named Tahlia, Imani, Sierra and Maya.
He used song lyrics he wrote as a teenager and the music generator Suno to make the music.
The group passed 100,000 YouTube subscribers in January and now has more than two million, with a large audience in Asia and Africa.
He says every video is labelled as AI-created and he is openly the human songwriter.
He says the project costs him more than it earns; Spotify will not put AI music on its official playlists.
quote_evidence: Now they have more than two million YouTube subscribers.
With the various online subscription fees, this is still costing me more than I make from it.
why_it_matters_hint: One person with AI tools built a fictional pop act with a large online audience, though not yet a profit.
notes: Subscriber figures come from Raybould himself, not independently checked; the headline's 'millions of fans' is his claim.
